subject: Control RPC reconnections after orchestrator rotation — customer update & follow-up
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.com>
To: Elena Cruz <elena@medtechsolutions.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Apr 2028 08:13:00 -0700
Subject: Control RPC reconnections after orchestrator rotation — interim note

Elena / team,

Quick update from our end: during the scheduled zero-downtime rotation of the orchestration agent in your private cluster (rollout window 07:45–08:05 PDT) we observed a transient spike in control-RPC reconnects across 7/12 nodes. The reconnects caused brief per-tenant metadata fetch delays and three short-lived 5xx errors for API requests that hit the affected control-plane proxies. We consider this an availability impact but not a data loss incident — no customer inference requests were dropped permanently.

What we did immediately:
- Rolled back the agent update on the 7 impacted nodes at 08:02 PDT.
- Applied a temporary backoff in the orchestrator to reduce parallel reconnection attempts.
- Captured full diagnostic bundles from the affected control-plane proxies and the orchestrator leader for timeline analysis (attached).

Impact summary for MedTech Solutions:
- Window: ~07:50–08:02 PDT (peak at 07:55)
- Visible effect: intermittent 5xx on control-plane-backed routes (3 requests returned 503/504 for ~90s)
- User-facing inference requests: no persistent failures; retries from your client SDK would have succeeded after the transient errors

Next steps we are taking (short term):
1) Runbook post-checks and a targeted fix for the reconnect storm (Aditya and infra team).
2) Follow-up bridge to review logs and agree on a permanent rollout strategy (can do today 11:00 PDT or tomorrow morning).
3) Share a short post-incident timeline + root-cause analysis within 24 hours.

Attached: redwood-diagnostics-20280418.tgz (filtered logs), orchestrator-timeline-20280418.csv

Apologies for the disruption — we know predictable upgrades are important. Monica is on the thread for CS coordination and to help with any customer-side telemetry you want us to inspect.

Thanks,
Diego Fernandez
Senior Technical Account Manager
Redwood Inference

Elena — thanks, good questions. Short answers up front then attachments.

1) Traces & request ids: Please send any request ids you have from 07:50–08:00 (example: rq_7b9f3a). We captured sampled traces on our side and we can correlate; preliminary traces show repeated 502s emitted by control-proxy while the node re-established watches against the aggregator.

2) Rollback status: Rollback completed at 08:02 PDT for the 7 impacted nodes. After rollback we saw reconnect rate return to baseline within ~40s. No action required from your SDK beyond normal retries/backoff. We will follow up with suggested backoff parameters if we recommend change.

Attached is a short timeline excerpt (orchestrator-timeline-20280418.csv) and the diag tar (redwood-diagnostics-20280418.tgz). Short timeline:
- 07:45 PDT: rollout started (parallelism=4 in canary group).
- 07:51 PDT: control-proxy on node-17 reported watch rejections; reconnects increased.
- 07:55 PDT: peak reconnects; some proxied requests returned 503.
- 08:02 PDT: rollback initiated & rollback completed at 08:02:30 PDT.

We recommend the following until a permanent fix is live:
- Keep rolling window parallelism at 1–2 for your clusters (we’ll make this the default for production in the short term).
- For SDKs: ensure exponential backoff is enabled for 5xx with jitter; we’ll provide suggested params.

I can join the 10:30 demo if helpful — will be on standby. Monica will coordinate any customer-facing notes.

Diego

Subject: Postmortem notes & proposed remediation (control-RPC storm)

Folks — following the diagnostic analysis I ran overnight: preliminary root cause is an interaction between the new agent's reconnection scheduling and our control-aggregator's watch fan-in behavior. When the agent restarted it attempted to re-establish watches in parallel without a stagger, which for this private deployment (higher watch density due to multi-tenant proxies) caused the aggregator to apply backpressure and return transient 502/503s.

Actionable remediation we propose:
- Short term (today): enforce staggered reconnection windows (randomized 0–60s) in the agent and reduce default rollout parallelism to 1. We already rolled a config change to the staging branch; we plan to push the hotfix to canary nodes tonight after validation.
- Medium term (2 weeks): add a server-side leaky-bucket on the aggregator to gracefully queue watch re-establishments and emit more descriptive transient error codes so clients can backoff more intelligently.
- Monitoring: we’ve added a control-reconnect-rate alert at 10x baseline and a dashboard widget for your tenant with per-node reconnect counts.

We’ll send an official postmortem with a timeline + RCA and the patch PR link once the canary passes. Diego / Monica: please coordinate scheduling for the maintenance window and customer comms. Elena: if you want a private runbook or an opt-in tuning config for MedTech (lower watch density), we can prepare that; let us know.

-Aditya
Principal Infrastructure Engineer
Redwood Inference
